classes.name: Oral atypical antipsychotics
classes.description: Second-generation oral antipsychotics: aripiprazole, quetiapine IR/ER, olanzapine, risperidone, ziprasidone, lurasidone (Latuda), paliperidone ER, cariprazine (Vraylar), brexpiprazole (Rexulti), lumateperone (Caplyta), asenapine, iloperidone, clozapine, olanzapine/samidorphan (Lybalvi).
classes.plainDescription: A daily pill for schizophrenia, bipolar disorder or add-on treatment for depression.

classes.name: Long-acting injectable antipsychotics
classes.description: Long-acting injectables: aripiprazole (Abilify Maintena, Abilify Asimtufii, Aristada), paliperidone palmitate (Invega Sustenna/Trinza/Hafyera), risperidone (Risperdal Consta, Perseris, Uzedy, Rykindo), olanzapine pamoate (Zyprexa Relprevv), haloperidol and fluphenazine decanoate.
classes.plainDescription: A shot every few weeks or months instead of a daily pill.

preferredAgent.sig: Schizophrenia: 10-15 mg once daily. Bipolar mania: 15 mg once daily. Max 30 mg/day for both. Add-on for depression: start 2-5 mg once daily, max 15 mg/day. Dose per indication (label).
preferredAgent.plainSig: One pill once a day; the dose depends on what it is treating.

records.preferredRestriction: PA via the antipsychotic class rule (PA Instructions p.3, p.70); the electronic PA program (p.8) approves automatically when claims history or diagnosis meet criteria. The PDL intro says antipsychotics are exempt from the PDL PA requirement; the two documents conflict.

paRequired.reason: Antipsychotic class PA applies (non-PDL drug class; PA Instructions p.3 and p.70); drug not individually listed
criteria: Ages 6+: appropriate diagnosis documented in the patient record, OR prescribed by a psychiatrist (adult or child/adolescent) or their CRNP/PA. No prior drug trials required.
Ages 6+: documented stable therapy on the requested drug for 60+ consecutive days.
Ages 6+ without a documented diagnosis: approved 3 months (adults) or 6 months (ages 6-18); a diagnosis is required for later requests.

Under age 6: chart notes with specific symptoms supporting the diagnosis, prescriber attestation that monitoring protocols (Attachment C) were followed, and literature if off-label. Stable therapy does not apply.
Electronic PA: antipsychotics are in the EPA program; a claim whose history meets criteria is auto-approved at the pharmacy. A rejected EPA claim is not a denial; submit a manual request.

records.verificationNote: Not a PDL class: no oral antipsychotic appears in the 07/01/2026 Reference Tool (text searched, pp.1-28) or the 04/01/2026 therapeutic-category PDL. Conflict: the 04/01/2026 PDL (p.1) says antipsychotics are exempt from the PA requirement, but the newer PA Instructions (eff. 10/01/2026) list Antipsychotic Agents among non-PDL drugs that require PA (p.3; criteria p.70). Resolved toward the newer document (PA required). Aripiprazole chosen as the standard generic oral antipsychotic; dose is the label starting dose, not printed in the document. Drug-level PA status for individual generics is inferred from the class rule. [Sonnet check 2026-11-02: PA Instructions (eff. 10/01/2026) re-fetched: URL returns 200 (614 KB); p.3 lists Antipsychotic Agents under "Non-PDL Drugs and/or Drug Classes to Require PA" and p.8 lists them in the electronic PA (EPA) program; p.70 criteria: diagnosis or psychiatrist prescriber, prior trials not applicable. The PDL intro says antipsychotic and HIV/AIDS drugs are exempt from the PDL PA requirement, so the two documents conflict; PA stays recorded because a class-level PA document names the class, but the claim is class-wide and EPA auto-approves when claims history/diagnosis meet criteria. Confirm at point of prescribing.]

preferredAgent.sig: Deep IM (gluteal) injection every 4 weeks. First dose: 10-15 times the daily oral dose if stabilized on 10 mg/day or less (10-20 times if higher or at risk of relapse); give no more than 100 mg in the first injection and the rest 3-7 days later (label).
preferredAgent.plainSig: A shot into the muscle about once a month, given at the clinic.

records.verificationNote: Read PDF pp.78-83 (Central Nervous System, Antipsychotics) by column position: tier number, Prior Authorization, Step Therapy, Dispensing Limits, ACA and Limited Distribution dots; verified visually on p.81. No Prior Authorization dot appears on any oral antipsychotic row. Dispensing Limits dot is on most generics; the quantity is not printed in this document, so no quantity limit is recorded. Preferred pick is quetiapine IR 25 mg (most commonly written generic oral antipsychotic; all generic picks are Tier 1 with the same flags); its dose is a titration starting point and the sig is standard label dosing, not printed. Secuado (asenapine transdermal patch, PDF p.82, step dot) is excluded as not oral. Lybalvi and other oral brands absent from the list (e.g., Abilify Asimtufii is injectable) were not recorded as excluded; the document does not say its list is complete. [Sonnet check 2026-11-02: Fanapt confirmed Step+Dispensing columns (not PA) on rendered p.79; haloperidol decanoate Tier 1 no flags.]

records.verificationNote: Read PDF pp. 38-41 (printed pp. 24-27) Antipsychotics table. Preferred pick: risperidone tablets 0.25-3 mg are tier 2 with QL 60 tablets/30 days and no PA (PDF p. 40). Every other oral atypical on the list is either PA for members 65+ (which is most of this Medicare population) or a no-PA tier 4-5 product (ziprasidone, cariprazine, lumateperone). Quetiapine IR and olanzapine are tier 2 but carry the 65+ PA, so they sit in paRequired. Strength and sig are standard label starting dosing, not printed on the list. Brands not on the list (Latuda, Uzedy, Rykindo) are not inferred as excluded; the list's front matter says to ask Member Services about drugs not shown. [Sonnet check 2026-11-02: reconfirmed in PDF - risperidone tab tier 2, QL only, no PA (the ODT and solution carry PA >=65); alprazolam tab tier 2, QL 120 (150 for 2 mg), no PA, no # flag.]
